name: Data Analyzer: Malformed checking rules are refused with HTTP 422 and name the column and rule
objective: Shows a mistyped rule is reported to the user instead of being silently ignored or causing a crash. Runs once per case per route (14 runs).
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key and the request-rate counters reset. The sample file is a made-up 3-row table (age: 10, 200, 30; colour: red, blue, green). No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send the sample file with one badly formed rule at a time to each route.
steps.data: Each case is sent to both analyze routes (file upload and inline data): min='zz'; min=null; max=true; allowed=5; allowed=[an object]; the whole rule for a column is a plain text; an unknown rule key 'minimum'.
steps.expected: Every one gets HTTP 422 (unprocessable); the message names the column in quotes (age or colour) and, except for the 'plain text rule' case, the rule key in quotes (min, max, allowed or minimum).

name: Data Analyzer: The rule error message does not repeat the bad value
objective: Shows rejected input is not reflected back to the caller.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key and the request-rate counters reset. The sample file is a made-up 3-row table (age: 10, 200, 30; colour: red, blue, green). No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send a rule whose min is the text 'SECRET-VALUE-123'.
steps.expected: HTTP 422 and the reply text does not contain 'SECRET-VALUE-123'.

name: Data Analyzer: Malformed column-type definitions are refused with HTTP 422
objective: Shows a schema (column types) with the wrong shape, or an unknown type name, is rejected rather than ignored. Runs 3 cases on both routes (6 runs).
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key and the request-rate counters reset. The sample file is a made-up 3-row table (age: 10, 200, 30; colour: red, blue, green). No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send the sample file with a bad schema to each route.
steps.data: Schema age = 5; age = 'blobtype' (a type name the system does not know; common names such as 'integer' are now accepted); age = ['int']
steps.expected: HTTP 422 and the message names the column 'age' in quotes.

name: Data Analyzer: Correct rules and schema still work and report the expected problems
objective: Shows the stricter checking did not break valid requests.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key and the request-rate counters reset. The sample file is a made-up 3-row table (age: 10, 200, 30; colour: red, blue, green). No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send the sample file with age in 0-120, colour in red/blue, and schema age=int, colour=str to both routes.
steps.data: Row with age 200 and colour 'green' break the rules
steps.expected: HTTP 200; the issues include a range violation on age and an invalid-category-value issue on colour.

name: Data Analyzer: Decimal-number rules and empty rules are still accepted
objective: Shows older valid rule shapes were not newly refused.
precondition: Server application loaded in the offline test harness with a made-up API key and the request-rate counters reset. The sample file is a made-up 3-row table (age: 10, 200, 30; colour: red, blue, green). No network and no AI model.

steps.action: Send rules age min 1.5 / max 99, and colour {} (empty) to both routes.

name: Data Analyzer: The quality checker reports a rule it cannot apply, rather than dropping it
objective: Shows an unusable rule appears as a visible problem instead of a hidden gap in checking.
precondition: Quality-check code run directly on a small made-up table; no server.

steps.action: Run the range check directly on a small table with age min='zz' and colour allowed=5.
steps.expected: The check does not pass, and there are exactly two 'rule invalid' issues: (age, min, min_not_numeric) and (c, allowed, allowed_not_list).

name: Data Analyzer: The checker still applies the valid half of a partly bad rule
objective: Shows one bad key does not switch off the good checks beside it.
precondition: Quality-check code run directly on a small made-up table; no server.

steps.action: Run the range check with age max=100 (good) and min=None (bad) on a table with values 1 and 200.
steps.expected: The issues include the text 'max <= 100' and also a 'rule_invalid' issue.

name: Data Analyzer: A non-object rule is flagged and a mixed-type allowed list does not crash
objective: Shows odd rule shapes give a result rather than an error.
precondition: Quality-check code run directly on a small made-up table; no server.

steps.action: Run the range check with column a rule = plain text 'x', and column b allowed = [1, 'x'].
steps.expected: An issue with reason 'rule_not_object' exists for column a, and an issue mentioning 'allowed_values' exists (so the check finished normally).

name: Data Analyzer: The final report shows an unusable-rule problem even though it has no row
objective: Shows the user is told a rule was NOT checked, in the report they actually read.
precondition: Quality-check and report-building code run directly on a small made-up table; no server.

steps.action: Run the whole quality pipeline with age min='zz' and build the report.
steps.expected: The report contains exactly one 'rule_invalid' issue, for column age, and its message contains 'NOT checked'.
